clue.text: Explorer drinks carafe, getting sloshed

indicators.note: sloshed means drunk and staggering, so the letters of the two words lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: An explorer gets drunk on a carafe of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting sloshed' rearranges DRINKS and CARAFE together; the drinking picture fits the sixteenth-century seafarer nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan navigator who sailed around the world, an explorer by any measure.

clue.text: Supporting part of the hospital in advance!

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
a ward is a room or section of a hospital

explanation.surface: A supportive hospital unit pushes ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward and in advance are synonyms describing position ahead of others.

clue.text: A provider of accommodation — not house, a workshop

indicators.note: not says the abbreviation for house is left out of the hotel-keeper

parts.note: a hotelier runs a hotel, providing rooms

explanation.surface: A hotel-keeper who has no house is reduced to a workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's studio, a kind of workshop.

clue.text: Whiskery creature, revolutionary boy, becomes popular

parts.note: a cat is famously whiskered
Che Guevara is the crossword's favourite revolutionary
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A whiskered cat and a rebellious lad both find fame.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch on is an idiom meaning to become fashionable or widely liked.

clue.text: Younger member of family, son, self-righteous person

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees
a prig is smugly moralistic

explanation.surface: The youngest child of the household is a sanctimonious son.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig, like a scion or offshoot, is a young descendant of a family.

clue.text: Whistle-blower has mounting hesitation — shut up or perk up?

parts.note: a referee, ref for short, blows the whistle

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means rising, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating
sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: A referee hesitates more and more, unsure whether to silence or encourage players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns ER into RE in this down clue. 'Whistle-blower' suggests an informer, but here it is the match official.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh someone is to revive or invigorate them, a synonym of perk up.

clue.text: Some working lethargically for minor ruler

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people work sluggishly for a petty monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'for'; that word is a link between wordplay and definition, so the definition is just 'minor ruler'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinglet is a petty or insignificant king, the diminutive suffix marking him as minor.

clue.text: Combination to maximise the possibility of a hold-up

definitions.text: Combination to maximise the possibility of a hold-up

parts.words: Combination to maximise the possibility of a hold-up
parts.note: a hold-up here is not a robbery but keeping trousers in place, using two supports at once

explanation.surface: A gang pairs up to make a robbery more likely.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means taking double precautions, literally wearing both a waist strap and shoulder straps.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a doubly secure trouser support and, by extension, any double safeguard.

clue.text: What a sucker may need

parts.note: a sucker here is literally someone sucking up a drink, not a gullible person

explanation.walkthrough: 'sucker' usually means a dupe; here it is a person sipping a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking tube is the instrument through which someone sucks up a beverage.

clue.text: Serious composer getting established all around

indicators.note: all around says the abbreviation for established surrounds the composer

parts.note: EST is the abbreviation for established, as on shop signs
Thomas Arne wrote Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A serious composer becomes well known everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest and serious are synonyms for a sincere, grave manner.

clue.text: Engineers needing better specialist for removing dross

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
finer means better

explanation.surface: Engineers need a superior expert to clear away rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A refiner purifies metals or sugar, removing impurities such as dross.

clue.text: Contemptible words with which to address good-looking girl?

definitions.text: words with which to address good-looking girl?
definitions.meaning: a letter for an attractive girl would be addressed ..., dish being slang for a beauty

explanation.surface: A slimy chat-up line for a pretty girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as TO A DISH, dish being slang for an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadish describes someone loathsome like a toad, hence contemptible.

clue.text: Fairy girl men led astray

indicators.note: something led astray goes off course, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A fairy girl leads some men off the path.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is a mischievous imaginary sprite, a kind of fairy blamed for mechanical faults.

clue.text: I run after man in the wrong direction — a low point

indicators.note: after puts the I and run letters behind the reversed name
in the wrong direction means the man's name is read backwards

parts.note: Dan is a man's name
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: I chase a man who heads off the wrong way at my lowest ebb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wrong direction' turns DAN into NAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, opposite the zenith.

clue.text: Motorway junction fare?

parts.note: fare is food, not a ticket price, and the junction is a famously tangled one

explanation.walkthrough: Spaghetti Junction is the nickname of a tangled motorway interchange in Birmingham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The pasta is food, and its name nicknames the knotted interchange near Birmingham.

clue.text: Various characters from Madras met in another capital

indicators.note: Various says the letters are taken in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: People from an Indian city gathered in a European capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is the capital of the Netherlands; another because Madras was once a capital too.

clue.text: Bishop and priest in items of clothing

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Annas was the Jewish high priest in the Gospels

explanation.surface: A bishop and priest are dressed in their vestments.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandannas are large patterned neckerchiefs, worn as items of clothing.

clue.text: Greek character's obvious description of some physics

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
clear means obvious

explanation.surface: A Greek figure plainly describes a branch of physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear physics studies atomic nuclei, so the adjective describes that branch of the science.

clue.text: Cleo's lover wants to get married? The opposite!

parts.note: Mark Antony was Cleopatra's lover

explanation.surface: Cleopatra's lover wants to wed, but gets the opposite answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word of opposite meaning.

clue.text: Only a slight accident, but Head of Police called

indicators.note: Head of picks the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: The police chief phoned in about a minor collision.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a minor car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A prang is informal British slang for a minor collision or bump.

clue.text: The old man wanting model — hugging old bag!

parts.note: pa is a familiar term for father, the old man

indicators.note: hugging means the model's word wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: to pose is to model

explanation.surface: Father wants a model embracing an old bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A papoose is a bag or pouch for carrying a baby on the back.

clue.text: A woman starts to knit some jackets

parts.note: Nora is a woman's name

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A woman begins knitting some jackets.
explanation.definitionFit: Anoraks are hooded waterproof jackets.

clue.text: A doubter, not quiet self-denying type

indicators.note: not means the music sign for quiet is dropped from the doubter

parts.note: a sceptic doubts
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A doubter, no longer quiet, practises self-denial.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic practises severe self-denial, abstaining from comforts.

clue.text: Stop part of tract digesting food

definitions.meaning: a punctuation mark that halts a sentence
the large intestine, part of the digestive tract

explanation.definitionFit: A colon is both a punctuation mark, a stop, and the main stretch of the large intestine.

clue.text: Deed of maybe ditched lover, one in conspiracy

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, maybe one dumped

indicators.note: in places the numeral one within the conspiracy word

parts.note: a plot is a conspiracy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A jilted lover's deed: joining a conspiracy.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit is a bold deed or feat.

clue.text: Outside, stealing a kiss, going on for ages

indicators.note: stealing means taking away the kiss from the outside word

parts.note: external means outside
X is the symbol for a kiss

explanation.surface: Outdoors, sneaking a kiss lasts forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means everlasting, continuing for ages without end.

clue.text: Display produced by famous designer and a man of no name

parts.note: Christian Dior was a famous French fashion designer

indicators.note: of no means the man is left without the abbreviation for name

parts.note: man taken as a word

explanation.surface: A famous designer and an anonymous man produce a display.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional scenic display, as in a museum.

clue.text: Two, three, …? There will be many more in this maths set!

definitions.text: Two, three, …? There will be many more in this maths set!

parts.words: Two, three, …? There will be many more in this maths set!
parts.note: the series continues five, seven, eleven, an infinite set of numbers with no divisors but one and themselves

explanation.walkthrough: Two and three begin the set; Euclid proved it never ends, hence many more.
explanation.definitionFit: Integers divisible only by one and themselves form this endless mathematical set.
